title: Maths #4 · The chain rule as three gears (F40 imitation of @learnara.math's 7.1× reel; white studio, loop)

captions.instagram:
Turn x once. How many times does y turn? 🤔

Class 12 Maths · Continuity and Differentiability: the chain rule
Maths, visualised #4

Three gears: x drives u, u drives y.
u turns 2× per turn of x → du/dx = 2
y turns 3× per turn of u → dy/du = 3
So one turn of x turns y 3 × 2 = 6 times. Not 3 + 2.
Rates along a chain multiply: dy/dx = dy/du · du/dx
